critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1177 POST /api/analytics/click silently returns {ok:false} for invalid asset_type instead of HTTP 400. Spec said 'asset_type validation rejects unknown values' — currently rejected but with 200 status. Frontends would not know to surface an error. Recommend HTTPException(400) on invalid asset_type for symmetry with GET /admin/analytics/top-clicks which returns 400.

server.py:1145 /admin/cms/search-destinations does not cap the response size of `q=''` (empty query) — returns up to 8 of each kind which is fine, but on a populated DB an empty `q` will return 40 docs total per request. Acceptable today (DB is empty per spec note) but consider requiring q.length >= 2 to avoid accidental large-set scans.

server.py:1100 ALLOWED_CATEGORY_FIELDS reused for both L1 categories and L2 subcategories. L2 subcategories cannot have their `l1_id` changed via PUT (correctly excluded), but the field 'order' is allowed on L2 even though subcategories may not have a meaningful per-L2 order today. Document or split the allow-list.

POST /api/analytics/click writes a Mongo doc per click without any rate limiting or de-duplication. A malicious user can balloon the asset_clicks collection. Recommend a TTL index + per-IP/per-session debounce on the consumer.

Backend FOLDER_MAP 'cms' entry — confirmed working (uploads under lokl/cms) but ensure the destructive Cloudinary cleanup migration (006) prefix-scans lokl/cms too, else orphan CMS images won't get garbage-collected.

Hero/Category/Offer 'redirect_url' is stored as a plain string with no validation. An admin could paste an external URL like 'https://evil.com' and the consumer would honour it (Next/Link will render an <a href>). Recommend a server-side allow-list (must start with '/' or match a known host).
